title: A Pact Against Gold-Plating the Research Exception?
content:
In the State of the EU address last week, Commission President von der Leyen announced, to some applause, the idea of a ‘Pact against gold-plating’.

This refers to when EU Member States implementing EU laws decide to add extra detail to the features of the official Regulation, Directive or other regulatory tool. While some of this is simple drafting to ensure EU laws fit seamlessly into national statute, sometimes it serves other goals, such as advantaging a given sector of that country’s economy.

The problem is that adding such provisions tends to make regulation more difficult to comply with. It also represents a barrier to cross-border collaboration by undermining harmonisation efforts.

Typically, efforts to address gold plating focus on things like product regulation or reporting requirements. However, the way in which national governments have implemented copyright exceptions – often under pressure from the entertainment sector – arguably provides another strong example.
